problem: The tenant-root table (the one whose id IS the group identifier - e.g. restaurant_groups, districts, organizations) has no group_id column to scope on by nature, since the row IS the group. By default it's either read: everyone (every authed user enumerates all tenants - leak) or read: admin (no tenant member can see their own tenant row - too tight). Neither composes correctly with act_as. When a tenant role is enough, no schema change is needed: on groups.bootstrap.org_table, `read: role:<tenant role>` (with groups.role_field) lets a holder read only their own tenant's row and answers 404 to members without the role (api({at:'access'}) → tenant_root_role_scope). Use the fix below when every member must read the row.
fix: Give the tenant-root table a self-referential group_id column that always equals its own id. Then it scopes like any other group-keyed table - a tenant member sees only their own row, an admin sees all, a stepped-in admin sees only the tenant they stepped into. The id<->group_id link is maintained by a one-line on_insert hook (the framework can't fill it at INSERT time because the row's id isn't known until after the insert).

recipe.1_schema: Add `group_id` to the tenant-root table. In schema.prisma: `groupId Int? @map("group_id")`. After deploy, run a one-time backfill: UPDATE <table> SET group_id = id WHERE group_id IS NULL.
recipe.2_hook: In hooks.yaml: on_insert: { restaurant_groups: [{ sql: "UPDATE restaurant_groups SET group_id = id WHERE id = {{id}} AND group_id IS NULL" }] }. Idempotent - the WHERE NULL guards against re-firing.
recipe.3_access: In app.yaml, flip the table from `read: everyone` (or admin) to `read: group`. Writes typically stay admin-only: `restaurant_groups: { read: group, write: admin, update: admin, delete: admin }`. If users found their own tenant through POST /api/_groups/create (this table is groups.bootstrap.org_table), declare `write: off` instead of `write: admin`: a declared `write: admin` also refuses the bootstrap for everyone but admins (403), while `off` leaves bootstrap as the only way to create a tenant.
recipe.4_act_as: Compose naturally - a stepped-in admin sees only the tenant they stepped into, because the WHERE clause becomes `group_id = <acting_as_group>` and the only row matching is the tenant-root row itself.
recipe.5_step_out: Frontends that cached the full-tenant roster while bypass was on should reload on step-out so the cache repopulates. (The server is right; the cache is stale.)

verified_pattern_for: restaurant_groups (multi-restaurant SaaS), districts (school-district apps), organizations / tenants / accounts (any generic multi-tenant root). Same shape works wherever the root table needs to be visible to its own members but not to other tenants.
